# Psalm 141 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-psalm of-David. O-YHWH I-have-called-you; hasten to-me; give-ear to-my-voice when-I-call to-you.

**2** Let-be-established my-prayer incense before-you, the-lifting-of my-hands offering-of evening.

**3** Set O-YHWH a-guard to-my-mouth; keep-watch over-door-of my-lips.

**4** Do-not incline my-heart to-thing evil, to-practice deeds in-wickedness with-men doers-of iniquity; and-not let-me-eat of-their-delicacies.

**5** Let-strike-me the-righteous — kindness; and-let-him-reprove-me — oil-of the-head let-not refuse my-head; for still and-my-prayer against their-evils.

**6** Are-thrown-down by-sides-of the-rock their-judges; and-they-will-hear my-words for they-are-pleasant.

**7** Like-one-plowing and-breaking in-the-earth, are-scattered our-bones at-mouth-of Sheol.

**8** For to-you O-YHWH Lord my-eyes; in-you I-take-refuge; do-not pour-out my-soul.

**9** Keep-me from-hands-of the-trap they-have-set for-me, and-from-snares-of doers-of iniquity.

**10** Let-fall in-his-own-nets the-wicked, together — while-I pass-by.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **141:2**: 'My-prayer incense... lifting-of my-hands offering-of evening' — prayer as spiritual sacrifice; internal worship replacing external ritual.

- **141:5**: Accepting righteous rebuke as 'kindness' and 'oil' — wisdom tradition: correction from the faithful is a gift, not an insult.

— EMET
